name: Crypto stress
summary: Bitcoin near $64,900 on 15 Nov, 25% below its 52-week high and 12% lower on the week; no stablecoin de-peg found
state: Bitcoin was near $64,865 at 05:40 UTC on 15 Nov, 25.1% below its 52-week high of $86,600, 12.0% lower on the week and 18.9% lower over a month (Yahoo Finance). Total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2bn, the largest contraction since 2022, but no peg broke (The Block, 11 Nov). The drawdown sits just past the 25% Watch line, and no top-10 exchange failure was found as of 15 Nov.
for_you: Crypto prices are falling sharply. Holders of crypto assets are directly exposed; crypto is largely unregulated in the UK and not covered by the FSCS.
rubric_hit: BTC drawdown 24.6% has not yet cleared the 22.5% exit line, so Watch holds

sources.title: The Block — Stablecoin supply drops $14.2 billion, largest contraction since 2022

why: Crypto is now plumbed into mainstream finance via ETFs and stablecoins; a crash or de-peg can spill into funding markets.
drivers: Liquidity, leverage, regulation, stablecoin reserves, exchange solvency.

rubric.alert: Drawdown > 45%, or a major stablecoin de-pegs (> 3% for > 24h), or a top-10 exchange fails.
rubric.watch: Drawdown 25–45%, or a top-10 exchange/stablecoin under stress.
rubric.normal: Bitcoin drawdown from 52-week high < 25% and no major stablecoin/exchange incidents.
